props.title: Elvis: That's the Way It Is

sections.content: Elvis: That's the Way It Is revolutionized concert documentaries by capturing Elvis Presley at his performing peak during his Las Vegas residency. The film showcases The King's magnetic stage presence and musical versatility as he rehearses and performs at the International Hotel. Unlike earlier rock docs like Monterey Pop (1968) or Woodstock (1970), this isn't just concert footage - it's an intimate portrait of an artist reclaiming his throne after his famous '68 Comeback Special. The documentary style influenced later concert films like The Last Waltz (1978) and Stop Making Sense (1984) in how it balanced performance with behind-the-scenes moments.

sections.content: The film's technical innovations were groundbreaking for 1970. Multiple camera setups captured Elvis from every angle, creating an immersive concert experience that became the template for modern music documentaries. The restoration work done for the 2001 Special Edition enhanced the original's vibrant cinematography while adding previously unseen footage. This influenced later restorations like The Beatles: Get Back (2021) in how it preserved and enhanced historical music footage.

Beyond just documenting performances, the film captures Elvis's personality and working process. We see him joking with his band, meticulously arranging songs, and interacting with fans. This blueprint influenced intimate artist portraits like Madonna: Truth or Dare (1991) and Justin Timberlake + The Tennessee Kids (2016), showing how a concert film could also be a character study. SUBHEAD: The Vegas Years Context

The film documents a crucial period in Elvis's career when Las Vegas residencies weren't yet considered artistic surrender. His International Hotel shows were innovative, mixing rock, country, and gospel with theatrical showmanship. This context is vital for understanding later Vegas-era music docs like Liberace: Behind the Music (1988) and the ways Elvis (2022) portrayed this period in Presley's biopic treatment.
